title: Integrated Assembly Manifest
text_faithful: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): the risen version gathers the whole vision — cube, wall, gates, foundations, street, radiance — into one city, presented as a single assembled version rather than scattered parts.
engineering: Engineering view: the integrated assembly manifest is the version index for this pair. It lists every assembled subsystem, its source record, its feasibility label, and its test result, so the version is auditable part by part. It is a manifest of a versioned model and prototype set, not a claim that a full-scale city stands.
body:
Public versioning practice includes manifest files, bills of materials, configuration management, and audit trails, all standard in engineering and software.

This manifest cross-links all fifteen Wave 1 pairs, so every subsystem in the version can be traced to its own pair record. Suite map: this record cross-links all fifteen Wave 1 pairs — new-jerusalem-light-city, jesus-risen-version, new-jerusalem-cube-city, new-jerusalem-jasper-wall, new-jerusalem-twelve-gates, new-jerusalem-twelve-foundations, new-jerusalem-golden-street, new-jerusalem-transparent-gold, new-jerusalem-pearl-gates, new-jerusalem-radiance-no-night, new-jerusalem-scripture-specification, new-jerusalem-measurement-scale, new-jerusalem-light-controls, new-jerusalem-gemstone-optics, new-jerusalem-energy-thermal-grid. Each pair is a separate database; later waves add parametric geometry, optical validation, structural feasibility, material substitution, manufacturing drawings, prototype planning, digital-physical comparison, evidence ledgers, technology families, and target/integration pairs.

engineering: Engineering view: freezing a specification means versioning it and locking its parameters for this version. Later versions may revise interpretations, but this version does not drift silently; every change becomes a new version with an audit entry.
body:
Public specification practice includes versioned requirements databases, constraint records, uncertainty flags, and freeze procedures with sign-off checklists.

The scripture-specification pair carries the full verse-to-parameter mapping, including the symbolism-to-architecture mapping and the interpretation comparison engine.

Real radiance practice includes emissive-surface rendering, exposure control, LED array specification, photometric testing, and glare analysis with published limits.

title: Energy Budget Closed
text_faithful: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): the city is lit without weariness, and the energy budget honors that picture by accounting for every watt the version actually uses.
engineering: Engineering view: an energy budget closes when total load fits its stated budget with margin, for a stated scope. This record closes the budget for the prototype and installation scope only; a full-scale city energy budget is a research problem, not a closed figure.
body:
Real energy practice includes load estimation, microgrid design, storage and backup sizing, cooling and heat rejection, and energy-balance computation.

The demo sums named loads against a stated budget and prints the margin, so closure is arithmetic.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Energy Budget Closed'


def main():
    print(TITLE + ' - working demo')
    loads = [('Gate lighting', 2400), ('Street lighting', 3600), ('Wall lighting', 1800), ('Controls and sensors', 600)]
    budget = 12000
    total = sum(w for _, w in loads)
    for name, w in loads:
        print('%s: %d W' % (name, w))
    print('Total load: %d W; budget: %d W; margin: %d W' % (total, budget, budget - total))
    print('Budget closed: ' + ('YES' if total <= budget else 'NO'))


main()

title: Glare Safety Passed
text_faithful: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): the city shines without harming the eye, and glare safety keeps that picture honest by measuring brightness against limits.
engineering: Engineering view: glare safety testing is demonstrated. Luminance values at viewing positions are measured or computed and compared against published limits, with margins reported. A radiant design that exceeds safe luminance fails, however beautiful its rendering.
body:
Real glare practice includes luminance measurement, glare analysis, photometric test reports, and glare-aware dimming in lighting controllers.

The demo compares named viewing positions against a stated limit and prints the worst-case margin.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Glare Safety Passed'


def main():
    print(TITLE + ' - working demo')
    values = [('Gate approach', 850), ('Street center', 1100), ('Wall viewing bay', 920), ('Plaza viewpoint', 780)]
    limit = 1500
    worst = max(v for _, v in values)
    for name, v in values:
        print('%s: %d cd/m2 -> %s (limit %d)' % (name, v, 'PASS' if v <= limit else 'FAIL', limit))
    print('Worst: %d cd/m2; margin: %d cd/m2' % (worst, limit - worst))


main()
